pairwise_assessment: MAIT is a lineage/subset label and CD8-GZMK is a marker-defined CD8 T-cell state; the shared markers are a granzyme cytotoxicity program. Flag for review because the MAIT source sentence says the cells expressed cytotoxic molecules except GZMB and GZMH, yet those genes are included in the extracted marker set.

Contractile SMCs and Mes3 both point to a contractile mesenchymal/smooth muscle program marked by ACTA2/TAGLN/MYL9. The difference is a descriptive cell-state label versus a study-specific mesenchymal cluster label.
KERA A and epidermis both map to keratinocyte/epidermal identity through KRT1/KRT10/KRT14. This is mainly nomenclature or cluster naming rather than a deep state difference.

Pericyte and vascular smooth muscle cell labels share contractile/mural markers ACTA2/TAGLN/RGS5. The relationship reflects the perivascular mural continuum and the ambiguity between cell type and contractile state.
PC is explicitly pericyte in the source context and vascular mural cell is a broader mural label; both use NOTCH3/PDGFRB/RGS5.
Smooth muscle cell and eMSC are linked by MCAM/SUSD2/PDGFRB, markers of endometrial mesenchymal stem-like cells. This suggests a stem-like mesenchymal state embedded in a smooth-muscle label.
EC is an abbreviation for endothelial cells; the shared markers CD144/AQP1/PECAM1 support the same endothelial lineage.
Fibroblast (COL1A1) and fibroblast clusters are both fibroblast labels anchored by extracellular matrix collagens. This is a subtype/broad-label naming difference.

Mac3 is a study-specific macrophage cluster distinguished by complement genes and CD163, while the neighbor is a classical macrophage label with the same markers. This maps a cluster code onto macrophage subtype biology.
Basal radial glia and outer radial glia are closely related progenitor labels anchored by TNC/FAM107A/HOPX. This is mostly nomenclature across developmental neurobiology contexts.
CD.Mono.FCN1.S100A4 is a marker-coded monocyte label and the neighbor is a classical monocyte label; the shared markers FCN1/S100A4/S100A6 map the coded label to monocyte identity.

Naive T-cell markers retrieve Treg.1 because the source states Treg.1 has elevated naive markers. This is not a cell-type identity match; it shows that a regulatory subtype can carry a naive-like state program.
TCM and Treg.1 share CCR7/SELL/TCF7/LEF1 because Treg.1 is described as naive-like. This links memory/naive state markers across regulatory and non-regulatory labels.
TN and Treg.1 share naive markers. The name difference reflects lineage/state layering: Treg.1 remains a regulatory cluster but carries a naive-like transcriptional program.
Treg.1 and naive/memory clusters share CCR7/SELL/TCF7/LEF1. This is a state-program bridge between a Treg subtype and broader naive/memory annotation.
Activated and activated TRM/TEM cluster are both activation labels using IFNG/CCL3/CCL4. This is a clean cross-study state match despite different specificity.
Pluripotent and iPSC labels are linked by canonical pluripotency markers NANOG/SOX2/POU5F1. This is a shared developmental state rather than a conflicting cell type.
Carcinoma cell and epithelial cell share epithelial markers EPCAM/KRT8/KRT18. The key context difference is malignant epithelial tumor compartment versus broad epithelial lineage.
Carcinoma cell and epithelial cell again share epithelial markers; the relationship is malignant context versus canonical epithelial annotation.
Carcinoma cell and epithelial share epithelial markers; this connects disease/tumor context to a broad epithelial lineage label.
Classical monocytes and MDSC share S100A8/S100A9/S100A12. The marker bridge captures an inflammatory/immature myeloid program that different studies name as classical monocyte or MDSC.
MDSC and macrophage/disease programs are linked through S100A8/S100A9/S100A12 alarmin genes. This is a disease-context myeloid state rather than a simple identity match.
Naive CD4 T cells and CT0b both express CCR7/SELL/TCF7/KLF2/LEF1; the CT0b context describes mostly central memory cells. This exposes the continuum between naive and central-memory labels.
Naive T cell and naive/memory are essentially different granularities of the same naive/memory marker program.
TCM and naive/memory share CCR7/SELL/TCF7/LEF1; the broader HCA label groups several clusters under naive/memory.
TN and naive/memory share the same naive markers; this is abbreviation/granularity rather than a distinct biological conflict.

LumHR epithelial cells and KRTs+ macrophages share keratin genes. This is biologically interesting but potentially confounded by epithelial RNA, phagocytosis, doublets, or keratin-positive macrophage annotation; it requires manual follow-up before using as a biological claim.
Naive T cells and CT0b are linked by naive/central-memory markers. The source calls CT0b central memory, so this is a state-continuum relation rather than exact identity.
Naive T cell and TCM share CCR7/SELL/TCF7/LEF1. The bridge captures the shared resting/central-memory axis, not necessarily identical T-cell states.
TN is a naive-like T-cell label; the shared markers support a straightforward abbreviation/state alias.
Mesenchymal stem cell and hTDSC share CD44/CD90/CD105. The relationship maps a general MSC marker panel onto tendon-derived stem cells.
Central memory T cell maps to a broader naive-or-TCM label using CCR7/SELL/TCF7. This is a granularity difference in resting CD4 T-cell states.

Regulatory T cell and Treg are the same concept; the marker overlap supports nomenclature harmonization rather than state discovery. The second snippet is not very specific and should be checked before using.
